h: Manchester's City Centre on Your Doorstep
p: Gamebox at the Arndale is especially handy if you're visiting Manchester with kids who need a break from shopping. The game selection includes options for younger children as well as more challenging rooms for older players, so take a look before booking and pick a theme that will grab everyone. Sessions don't take long, making it easy to fit into a busy day in town.

Once your game is done, there's an awful lot within a few minutes' walk. The National Football Museum sits in the striking glass Urbis building at Cathedral Gardens, just across from the Arndale, and it's packed with interactive exhibits, famous shirts and trophies. Football fans of all ages will love it, whatever team they support.

Next door, Manchester Cathedral is a beautiful medieval building worth a look inside, and close by is Chetham's Library, founded in 1653 and one of the oldest public libraries in the English-speaking world. A short walk the other way along Deansgate brings you to the John Rylands Research Institute and Library, a stunning neo-Gothic building that looks like something out of Harry Potter.

For something hands-on, the Science and Industry Museum in Castlefield tells the story of Manchester's role in the Industrial Revolution and the birth of the computer age. Castlefield itself, with its canals and old railway viaducts, is a lovely spot for a drink or a walk. Getting about is simple: the Metrolink tram stops at Market Street and Shudehill are close to the Arndale, and Manchester Victoria station is just a few minutes away. If the weather's kind, the green lawns of Cathedral Gardens and Exchange Square right outside are a good spot to sit with a drink and watch the city go by.
